notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Long white plates with a blue strip on the left, like most of Europe.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Letters Ç, Ş, Ö, Ü and Ğ, plus a dotless lowercase i and a dotted capital İ; the dotless one is nearly unique.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: Plain thin white rectangular bollard with one red reflector on the front. A rare yellow one appears in snowy areas.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: Mostly white lines, but yellow or mixed yellow-and-white lines are not unusual.

notes.subject: street
notes.text: Many roads have grainy "salt and pepper" asphalt.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Divided highways are extremely common, far more than in other Mediterranean countries.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Chevrons are usually red on white, the arrow tip not touching the edge; some have a neon yellow border.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: A black-and-yellow chevron with several upward arrows is common at junctions.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Narrow red-and-white chevrons also occur; nearly identical ones exist in South Africa.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Direction signs use a distinctive font with noticeably wide letter spacing.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Snow poles run black, orange, black, white from top to bottom, with small red reflectors.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Stop signs read "DUR", unique to this country.

notes.subject: guardrail
notes.text: Both A-type (rounded) and B-type (square) guardrails are used, which rules out most southern European and Middle Eastern countries.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Metal poles shaped like a ladder or with a mesh pattern are extremely common.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Generation 3 coverage never shows an antenna.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Generation 4 mostly uses a white car with only a sliver visible, with a short antenna or none.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: A grey pickup truck appears in some Generation 4 coverage; Georgia and several African countries have similar ones.

notes.subject: vegetation
notes.text: Arid in the southeast, Mediterranean in the southwest, lush forest in the north; typical is semi-arid farmland with few trees.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Tall, boxy apartment blocks are very common.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Mosques with tall minarets appear in most towns.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Brick paving is common in towns, in one typical brick shape.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Area codes start with 2 in the west and rise to 4 in the east; codes starting with 5 are not regional.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Kilometre markers show O- or D-road numbers, or on provincial roads the two-digit province code, which mostly rises alphabetically.

notes.subject: coverage
notes.text: Generation 4 truck coverage is mainly in the far east and along the south coast.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The north is much lusher and more forested than the rest of the country.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Treeless grassy valleys between round hills mark the northeast; Generation 3 shows very deep green grass.

notes.subject: vegetation
notes.text: Tea plantations are common in Rize province.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Tiled roofs dominate in the west two thirds, flat roofs in the southeast, and metal roofs in the east.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Low pyramid-shaped sheet metal roofs are mainly in the far east around Lake Van.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Large pale, uneven sandstone bricks are used in buildings in Nevşehir province.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Round white tanks are in the southeast; stacked horizontal-on-vertical tanks follow the south coast; vertical tanks are rare on the south and west coasts.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Dark blue, outward-bulging street signs, often with the city emblem on top, mark Izmir province.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Blue street signs with a small rounded top are used in the capital's province.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Whitewashed flat-roofed houses with blue accents or bare stone walls are typical around Bodrum.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Tall sandstone monoliths with ancient carved dwellings mark Göreme.
